company.name: Britannia Industries Limited
company.description:
Britannia Industries Limited is a prominent Indian food and beverage company founded in 1892 in Kolkata. It specializes in bakery, dairy, and snacking products and operates in over 80 countries. As part of the Wadia Group, Britannia has grown to become a household name in India, employing over 4,500 people and achieving a market capitalization of ₹1.08 trillion.

The company's diverse product portfolio includes a wide range of biscuits under popular brands like Good Day, NutriChoice, and Bourbon, as well as breads, cakes, and rusk products. In the dairy segment, Britannia produces milk, butter, cheese, ghee, and curd, with offerings like Winkin' Cow. With annual revenues exceeding ₹9,000 crore, Britannia maintains a strong market presence in the food and beverage sector, focusing on providing tasty yet healthy products that fit into consumers' daily lives.

outreach.subject: Britannia's operations + AI — quick thought
outreach.body:
Hi Ajay,

Britannia moves an enormous volume of SKUs across India daily, and I imagine keeping production efficiency and supply chain visibility tight is a constant balancing act at that scale. A lot of F&B manufacturers we speak with are starting to quietly pilot AI-driven demand forecasting and ops automation — not as a big transformation project, but as small, targeted wins that reduce waste and improve fill rates. Given your dual role across Operations and Technology, I thought it might be worth a 20-minute conversation to share what's working for similar companies and get your take on where Britannia is focusing. Would next week work for a quick call?
outreach.reasoning: Ajay holds both an Operations and CTO title, meaning he sits at the intersection of technology decisions and day-to-day operational accountability — a rare and powerful combination to address simultaneously. By referencing Britannia's massive distribution scale (a publicly known operational complexity), the email demonstrates genuine context rather than generic flattery. Anchoring the AI angle around practical, incremental wins (demand forecasting, waste reduction) rather than hype respects his seniority and avoids the 'big transformation' fatigue common at large FMCG companies. The CTA is low-commitment and framed as a value exchange (sharing what works + getting his perspective), which reduces friction for a busy executive.
